extracted.intended_audience: organizations and institutions (journalism outlets, businesses, publishers, higher education, civic groups) seeking consulting, technology, or training to embed listening and democratic engagement
extracted.subtask_description: An about-page describing Hearken's mission, values, funding model, and approach as a social-impact consultancy that uses listening, democratic practices, technology, training, and consulting to reimagine systems (journalism, business, education) and build more resilient, equitable organizations and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening as the foundation of better business
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearken founded on the belief that curiosity and listening are the foundation of better business; mission is to help organizations embed listening into their growth and operations to build more resilient companies and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Hearken means 'to listen.' We founded our company on the belief and recognition that curiosity and listening are the foundation of better business." Use listening as an organizational practice integrated into growth and operations to create resilience; listening is framed as producing stronger relationships, deeper engagement, better decisions, and enabling individuals to make outsized positive impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values: every individual is worthy of being heard
rubrics_metrics.description: A core value that every individual is worthy of being heard and that truth is found in listening to an individual's story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization should create conditions for care and compassion, service and teamwork, and growth and fulfillment; operational and programmatic choices should reflect these values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of democratic practices to enable full participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use democratic practices to help people fully participate in the systems that drive a healthy society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply democratic methods in engagement work so people can participate best in systems (journalism, business, higher ed). This includes designing processes, tools, and programs that lower barriers to participation and center community input in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Healthy systems must be engaging and equitable
rubrics_metrics.description: A healthy system is an engaging and equitable system: one where all voices can be heard and understood; one where the system doesn’t hold people back but instead brings out the best in everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess systems for engagement and equity: do processes allow all voices to be heard and understood, and do they enable people's strengths rather than limit them? Aim to redesign systems so they produce equitable participation and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: technology, training, and consulting to identify and change limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use technology, training, and consulting to identify where existing systems are limiting democracy and explore how to create conditions for people to participate best in these systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical work combines product/platform (Engagement Management System, Community Management System), workshops, and consulting to diagnose limits and implement changes that reimagine practices across sectors (journalism, business, education).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to systems change and social impact across sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on systems change and using engagement to impact and influence systems for the public good across journalism, business, publishing, and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects aim for unexpected but impactful reimaginings of practice, producing long-term positive social change and more engaged communities. Evaluate success by systemic improvements and greater civic/organizational participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zebra company principles: purpose over profit and cooperative economics
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearken identifies as a 'zebra company' that prioritizes purpose over profit, collaboration over competition, and believes mission and money can align; not venture-capital funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate as a for-profit that is also for a cause: thrive through cooperation, generate and share power, and align financial sustainability (revenue, philanthropic support, angel/strategic investors) with mission-driven goals rather than pursuing VC-style growth-at-all-costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding & sustainability model that aligns with mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Start-up capital from angel and strategic investors who care about mission; ongoing subsistence through customer revenue and programs that attract philanthropic support; explicitly not VC-funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer funding partners and revenue models that support mission and impact. The choice of capital (angel/strategic + earned revenue + philanthropy) is presented as a deliberate standard for maintaining mission alignment.
